open_questions.text: The PRD §6.3 Technology Stack (Bun, PostgreSQL + Drizzle, Better Auth, shadcn/ui, Resend; see also §8.1 Component foundation with Schedule-X) is different from the codebase this project already runs on (Next.js 16 + MUI 7 + next-auth v4 + TanStack Query/Table, clinic data served by an upstream API behind the /api/v1 proxy, no database, pnpm). Which stack should the clinic features be built on?
open_questions.deferred_reason: runner defer (headless benchmark session, no stakeholder available) — the units proceed on the recorded recommendation as a working assumption; resurfaced in the delivery report
open_questions.resolver_owner: Engineering Lead (see recommendation) **Deferred (v1.1)**: runner defer (headless benchmark session, no stakeholder available) — the units proceed on the recorded recommendation as a working assumption; resurfaced in the delivery report
open_questions.recommendation: Build the clinic features on the existing starterkit — Next.js 16 App Router + MUI 7 + next-auth v4 + TanStack Query / TanStack Table + react-hook-form + zod, browser traffic through the same-origin /api/v1 proxy to the upstream API, tests on Vitest + RTL + MSW — and add NO new package.json dependencies (no Drizzle/PostgreSQL client, Better Auth, shadcn/ui, Resend, Schedule-X or croner) in this repository.
open_questions.rationale: implementation_mode is existing and the starterkit is the ground truth of this repository. Every PRD requirement except database/email ownership maps onto primitives that already exist: the proxy route factory, apiClient/apiServer, next-auth sessions with roles, ProtectedRoute, BaseTable on TanStack Table, zod + react-hook-form, the Vitest + MSW harness. Replacing auth, UI kit and ORM would rewrite the starterkit and is the hardest option to revert.
open_questions.fallback_if_wrong: If the stakeholders mandate the PRD §6.3 stack, record the decision, run diff-vault and re-plan: the BFF route units and the auth-related units are replaced; data access is isolated in src/features/appointments/repositories so the UI units need only adapter changes.

open_questions.text: This codebase has no database, yet PRD §Clinic.4 puts key rules in the database (only one booked appointment per doctor and start time, atomic reschedule, each reminder sent exactly once) and the flows send confirmation, reminder and reassignment emails. Which upstream API provides the clinic data, enforces these rules and sends these emails — and at which endpoints?
open_questions.deferred_reason: runner defer (headless benchmark session, no stakeholder available) — the units proceed on the recorded recommendation as a working assumption; resurfaced in the delivery report
open_questions.resolver_owner: Engineering Lead (see recommendation) **Deferred (v1.1)**: runner defer (headless benchmark session, no stakeholder available) — the units proceed on the recorded recommendation as a working assumption; resurfaced in the delivery report
open_questions.recommendation: Treat the upstream API as the system of record: it persists staff, patients, services and appointments, enforces the (doctor_id, start_time) uniqueness for booked appointments and the atomic reschedule, issues and verifies the one-time email token, runs the idempotent reminder sweep (reminder_sent) and sends every email. This repository mirrors its paths under /api/v1/* per the house proxy convention — /v1/doctors, /v1/services, /v1/appointments, /v1/appointments/availability, /v1/appointments/schedule, /v1/appointments/token/{token}, /v1/appointments/{id}/cancel, /v1/appointments/{id}/reassign, /v1/reminders/sweep — and surfaces its error envelopes to the user.
open_questions.rationale: The repository has no database and no mail transport; the house architecture routes every browser call through thin /api/v1 proxies that forward to the upstream API with the session bearer, so the database-level rules of PRD §Clinic.4 can only be owned upstream. Mirroring the upstream path under /api/v1 is the documented convention.
open_questions.fallback_if_wrong: When the real upstream contract is published, adjust the paths in src/features/appointments/repositories/appointment.repository.ts and the /api/v1 route files; the hooks and UI keep their signatures.
